blocks.text: The Richter scale, the pH of a solution and the decibel scale all use logarithms, because each one compresses an enormous range into small, readable numbers. Once you see that a logarithm is just an index in disguise, the whole topic opens up.

blocks.title: Logarithm
blocks.text: $\log_a N = x$ means exactly the same as $a^x = N$. In words: the logarithm is the power to which the base must be raised to give the number. So $\log_2 32 = 5$ because $2^5 = 32$.

blocks.caption: Index form and logarithmic form say the same thing

blocks.markdown:
Reading between the two forms is the single most useful skill in this topic. Practise it in both directions:

- $2^5 = 32$ becomes $\log_2 32 = 5$
- $10^3 = 1000$ becomes $\log_{10} 1000 = 3$
- $\log_3 81 = 4$ becomes $3^4 = 81$

When no base is written, base 10 is assumed. So $\log 100 = 2$.

blocks.caption: The laws of logarithms mirror the laws of indices exactly

blocks.markdown:
### Why the laws look like the index laws

Because a logarithm **is** an index. Multiplying two numbers adds their indices, so it adds their logarithms. Dividing subtracts. Raising to a power multiplies.

This is also the historical reason logarithms were invented: they turn hard multiplication into easy addition.

blocks.title: Using the product and quotient laws
blocks.prompt: Evaluate log₁₀ 45 + log₁₀ 2 − log₁₀ 9 without a calculator.

steps.text: Addition of logs means multiplication of the numbers.
Subtraction of logs means division of the numbers.
The log of the base is always 1.

blocks.markdown:
### Logarithmic equations

Collapse the logarithms into a single logarithm first, then convert to index form.

For $\log_2 x + \log_2 (x - 2) = 3$: the product law gives $\log_2 \big(x(x-2)\big) = 3$, so $x(x - 2) = 2^3 = 8$. That gives $x^2 - 2x - 8 = 0$, hence $x = 4$ or $x = -2$.

blocks.title: Check for invalid solutions
blocks.text: You cannot take the logarithm of a negative number or of zero. In the example above, $x = -2$ must be **rejected** because $\log_2(-2)$ does not exist. Only $x = 4$ is a solution. Examiners award a mark specifically for rejecting the impossible root.

blocks.title: Negative logarithms mean numbers below 1
blocks.text: $\log_{10} 0.001 = -3$, because $10^{-3} = 0.001$. If a question gives you a number less than 1, expect a negative logarithm — that is a useful sanity check on your answer.

points: $\log_a N = x$ means the same as $a^x = N$; convert freely between the two forms.
When no base is shown, the base is 10.
Adding logs multiplies the numbers; subtracting logs divides them.
$\log(M^k) = k \log M$, which turns powers into multipliers.
$\log_a 1 = 0$ and $\log_a a = 1$ for every valid base.
Collapse to one logarithm before converting to index form, and reject any root that makes a logarithm undefined.
